The App Model

The App Model

Built 9 November 2026 from the pinned prototypes (N558), the code on main and the decisions to N568

The developer's reference for the whole WillpowerLab app (N574): one clickable phone with every user story beside it, to compare with the code; pinned in the repo as docs/design/app-model-<date>/ once pinned. The phone shows the way in, the first Take, the walk, Will's chat, the Ideal Text, the next Take, the chats with people, matching, the plan, Settings and Tokens; the coach's side (Marta's queue, the blind Judge, the cure, the founder's rows), the principles, and a customer's request with its answer. Every look and every word on the phone comes from the code on main or a signed decision; the dashed notes and the dark toasts are the model's own, not the app's.

How to use this model

This is the developer's reference (N574): read a story, press Show, compare the phone with the code, and fix the code where they differ. The founder's decisions log wins: where the code on main and a decision disagree, the decision is in force and the code is a bug to fix (backend docs/SPEC-DECISIONS-LOG.md, the newest entry first). Read every story as a test: press Show, and the phone opens that story's screen, to check against the files the story names. A red chip, "Code differs", marks a spot where the code still says what a decision replaced; a dashed note marks what is decided but not built. Pick a business and a journey to walk the app from its start, and "Whose phone" to see the other person's side.

Decisions drawn on the phone

  • N557 (9 November): the fix opens "And here's one moment to try another way:"; a good Take says "The rest of this Take held up just as well.". Built on main (frontend #1317).
  • N559 (9 November): the business community, offered once while Take 1 is processed with Join and Not now (its question is the model's draft, for the founder's OK, marked on the phone); the best fit first on who hears the next Take, drawn with Tomek and Artur; the suggested person comes from the business community and, by how people speak, a step ahead (red chip MATCH-05 / MATCH-09); the Settings card "Matching by how you speak".
  • N564 (the plan, logged 9 November): three levels of four Takes; each Take fills one of the level's four marks; no practice days, no "every day", no deadline row; after the third level, the summary session, then new levels. The card, the bar after the walk, a practice day's hello, the sheet and the plan's end are drawn so, dashed, with red chips PLAN-01, PLAN-07, PLAN-09, PLAN-10 and PLAN-12 where the code still draws "Your deadline", "15 minutes, 3 times a week", "{n} of {total} practices done." and "See you tomorrow.". Nobody is asked "When is your deadline?".
  • N565 item 7 (9 November): the praise opens with how it sounded to us: "To our ears, this one sounded really sure." or "To us, this one sounded really sure.", in turn. Built on main (frontend #1328). When the founder turns rings.WALK_VOICE on, Will writes the walk's lines by the founder's rules (services/prompts/walk_voice.py); the model draws the signed lines it falls back to.
  • N561 item 1, as N568 amends it (next app build): signed in, the iPhone app opens straight on the chats; signed out, on the first page (N471 item 4 stands). A dashed note on the app's first page.
  • N511 item 1 (4 November): the founder's admin ☰ has Training corpus under Data, beside Project deletions. The code (AdminMenu.tsx, FE #1256) moved it to Overview in the Roadmap's place, which no decision says: drawn as N511 has it, red chip COACH-12.
  • The line under a sent Take reads "Everyone in my list" when everyone is ticked (walkThread.ts peopleLine, NextTakeShareScreen.tsx allOn), where the pinned page showed the name.

Words with no source

One: the community question of N559 item 1, which the decision leaves to be drafted for the founder's OK; it is marked so on the phone. The people's names, roles, sayings and the coach's words are the prototype's examples, as in the pinned pages. Sample content, never the app's words: the library's exercises and the corpus imports are the locked coach panel prototype's; the Sunday note's case, the principles held, the strength and its notes, and the why are the code's own test examples; Sarah's request, Ariel's answer, the treatments and their prices are the customer-request prototypes'. The consent sentence on the widget's form is counsel's to write, so it is shown as a placeholder.

    What version 2 changes

    Your note: "this is a part that we apply to everyone ... it should be your first official take ... whatever questions we have for the first timer, we need to put them into slides."

    1. Will's welcome, then one big black button. Four bubbles (N492): "Hi {name}, and welcome. …", what the first Take is, Wozniak and Jobs, where to record. The button is "Start your first recording".
    2. The first Take: five questions are the slides on the recording screen, drawn as the poster (N462): Your field · Worth sharing · Who it's for · A moment · Your one thing. No set-up: the questions are the deck.
    3. While it is processed, the labels sit in a thin row at the top of Will's chat. Will: "While your feedback is being prepared, check what I heard." Then, one tap each: "Here's how others will see you", the plan, the agreement, "You're set".
    4. The walk opens when it's ready. Its row on top turns orange. On Take 1, the walk works on how the questions were answered: their best moment, one thing to improve, the helper words, "Lesson done." Then Will's one question and the Ideal Text, one paragraph per question.
    5. Then "Record Take 2" for the real talk: the feelings check with its Skip, then the set-up (the topic from the plan, length, slides).
    6. Moved: the plan's questions in Will's chat (N319) are now slides. N564 (9 November): nobody is asked "When is your deadline?"; only someone who chose "Prepare a talk" in the first choice (N572, N573) is asked "When is it?", with "No date yet": drawn, decided, not built.
    7. Gone: gap 5, the two hellos. Will says hi once.

    Locked as N401 on 3 November 2026; N462 and N492 have since changed the slides and the welcome, and this pin draws them. The step-by-step version is on its own page: The first Take.

    The gaps, and how each is covered

    What the map found in the code, each with its cover. The tag says what it needs.

    1. The default ring.To decideA new account gets ring 2. The chats and the join link need ring 6. Cover: you set the default ring for the launch. This prototype shows what ring 6 sees.
    2. The welcome shows again after signing up on the web.Gone (N471)The first page is design B: no "Enter the lab", and a signed-in person goes straight to the acceptance screen.
    3. A join link needs ring 6 from the person joining too.To decideOtherwise the join is refused without a word and no chat is made. Cover: the link brings its own access, so whoever joins through it gets the chats.
    4. The setup isn't built.To buildNothing in the code yet: no voice-note card, no agreement in the setup. Cover: N378, version 3, slotted in as shown, without the teams (N471).
    5. Two hellos in a row.Gone in version 2The plan's hello is no longer in Will's chat: the questions are slides. Will says hi once.
    6. Signing up with no link and no code.Gone (N471)No link means the waitlist, and there are no codes: Will never asks which team.
    7. A guest who signs up after Take 1.Gone (N471)There is no guest path: nobody records without an account.
    8. The join page says "Join".Covered hereThe signed "Join with your {company} account" (N335) needs a company's own sign-in, which is an integration (N378 item 7). Cover: "Join" stays until a company has one.
    9. No Microsoft sign-in.Signed, not builtBuilt today: WhatsApp, Email, Google and LinkedIn, plus Apple in the app. RASP's people sign in with Microsoft. Signed with N401 (items 6 and 7): a "Microsoft" button beside Google.
    10. Demo chats for a real newcomer.To decideOn the web, a ring-6 newcomer with an empty list gets two demo chats, "Sarah" and "Ariel", that aren't real. Cover: demo chats only for test accounts. A newcomer's list shows Will and "Add someone to chat with", as the iPhone app already does.
    11. In the iPhone app, a join link opens Safari.To buildThere are no universal links yet. Cover: universal links for willpowerlab.com/c/, so the app opens on the join page.
    12. The ask link has no page.To buildIts words are signed (N313), but /a/ is not built. Cover: the page as on the setup prototype.
    13. Coaches are still a list kept by hand.To buildCover: WillpowerLab's coach link, with the pass code inside, makes someone a speaking coach (N352).
    14. Two kinds of code.Gone (N471)There are no community codes and no open communities: a person's link is the one way in.
